First, note that

$$
\frac{3}{{[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\theta )]}^{4}}=3{[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\theta )]}^{-4}.
$$

De Moivre's Theorem states that

$$
{[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\phi )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\phi )]}^{n}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\phi )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\phi ).
$$

In our expression, we have $n=-4$ and $\phi =\theta .$ Substituting in these values, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{{[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\theta )]}^{4}} & =3{[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\theta )]}^{-4} \\  & =3[\operatorname{cos}⁡(-4\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-4\theta )].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the fact that $\operatorname{cos}⁡(-\phi )=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\phi )$ and $\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\phi )=-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\phi )$ for any input $\phi ,$ we have

$$
3[\operatorname{cos}⁡(-4\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-4\theta )]=3[\operatorname{cos}⁡(4\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4\theta )].
$$
